a.title: The Era of Doers: Stop Overthinking It
a.speaker: Francesco Ciulla
a.desc: Do you feel the same? AI has made it very easy to think a lot and build very little. Every week there is a new model, a new tool, a new workflow, and a new debate about the future of us developers. Ok, that is interesting, but at some point we still have to open the editor, build something, test it, ship it, and learn from it. Even using AI, but please, stop overthinking it and dedicate more time to do do something useful. Who experiment, connect ideas, build small things, break them, improve them, and keep moving are the ones who are gonna make it.

a.title: Taste: A Deep Dive
a.speaker: Tejas Kumar
a.desc: What even is the role of JS anymore? Do we still present users with carousels, tabs, cards, and the regular design primitives we've become familiar with? Or is this evolving? In this talk, we will explore how UX is changing and how to build for the agentic future.

a.title: The Ultimate Guide to Browser-Based AI: Privacy-First, Offline-Ready, and Fully Future-Proof
a.speaker: Maxim Salnikov
a.desc: Generative and intelligent features are quickly becoming a core part of modern web experiences—but they often come with trade-offs: privacy concerns, reliance on internet connectivity, and the cost of using cloud-based APIs. What if you could bring powerful AI directly into the browser, on the user's device? In this session, we’ll explore the full landscape of browser-based AI and machine learning—no servers required. From text generation and image recognition to real-time transcription and offline copilots, the web platform now provides a rich toolbox of APIs and tools to enable truly private, performant, and intelligent experiences.

b.title: Atomic State Strategies for Complex UIs: Beyond the Global Monolith
b.speaker: Fanis Prodromou
b.desc:
As Angular applications grow, our state management often follows one of two paths: a bloated, boilerplate-heavy global store or a complicated "God Component" managing dozens of RxJS streams or reactive signals. When you add complex requirements—like multi-layered filters, dynamic UI "pills," and bi-directional URL synchronization—the cracks in these traditional patterns begin to show.

In this talk, we will explore a fundamental shift in architecture: Atomic State Patterns.

By leveraging the power of Angular Signals, we can move away from monolithic state objects and toward decentralized, high-performance "atoms" of logic. We will live-architect a real-world filtering system, demonstrating how to:
- Deconstruct the Monolith: Break down complex filter states into independent, composable Signal units.
- Master the URL Bridge: Create a "Source of Truth" where the URL and local UI state are perfectly synced without race conditions.
- Harness Derived State: Use computed() signals to automatically generate UI elements like "Filter Pills" without manual subscription management.

a.title: WebMCP in Practice: Shipping MCP Severs in Browser
a.speaker: Tamas Piros
a.desc:
Every MCP tutorial puts the server on a server. They don't have to. If your app already has the data, the auth, and the UI state, why are you copying it to a backend just so an agent can reach it? WebMCP lets MCP servers run in the browser, right where the user already is. Almost nobody is doing this in production. I am. In this hands-on workshop, we'll build a WebMCP server from scratch in TypeScript and ship it inside a real web app.

I'll use Watch Anchor, my production deployment, as the reference case study, then walk you through the architectural decisions, the gotchas, and the parts the documentation doesn't cover yet. You'll leave with a working WebMCP server, a clear sense of when browser-native MCP beats server-side, and the patterns to deploy it in your own app on Monday.

b.title: Pear - Deploy Apps Device-to-Device without Servers
b.speaker: David Mark Clements
b.desc: For almost every application that currently exists, servers are no longer necessary. Terminal, desktop & mobile apps can receive over-the-air updates device-to-device. Apps can talk device-to-device. Apps can be deployed and used without servers, without the cloud, even without the internet. The server is the chokepoint. The server is the vulnerability. The server is the backdoor. This talk will demonstrate what Pear and its ecosystem makes possible, revealing refreshing new ways to build.

a.title: Models Gone Rogue: Securing AI Integrations
a.speaker: Elena Calvo Carazo
a.desc:
Your team ships an AI-powered feature. Users love it. Velocity looks great.

Then reality hits.

On Monday, a user crafts a prompt that leaks internal data. Incident response takes over the week.
On Tuesday, API costs spike far beyond forecasts. A budget review follows.
On Wednesday, an audit finds customer PII in logs. Legal and compliance get involved.

These scenarios are happening across the industry as AI integrations become mainstream. Disguised as simple-looking API calls, LLMs introduce new risks that break traditional security assumptions. The good news is that, as developers, we sit at the gateway for these vulnerabilities, and we can prevent them before shipping to production.

In this session, we will walk through what calling an AI API looks like in practice and why natural language input and unpredictable outputs expand the attack surface, before exploring four real-world vulnerability categories:

1. Prompt Injection: When users manipulate AI into changing its behaviour.
2. Malicious Output: Why applications shouldn't blindly trust what models return.
3. Denial of Wallet: How unbounded usage silently drains API budgets.
4. Data Spillage: When sensitive information leaks beyond intended boundaries.

For each category, we will explore concrete attack scenarios followed by practical defensive patterns, illustrated with visuals, demos, and code examples drawn from hands-on experience building AI integrations.

Throughout the session, we will return to a central idea: no single defence is enough. Securing AI integrations requires a defence-in-depth approach, where multiple layers work together to reduce risk and limit impact.

You'll leave with security patterns you can apply today as AI becomes a permanent part of the web stack.

b.title: Beyond Linting: Building an AI Code Reviewer Grounded in Architectural Mental Models
b.speaker: Evangelia Mitsopoulou
b.desc:
Most AI code review tools are good at catching bugs and style issues. But they miss a harder question: does this code reflect good architectural decisions, or just working code?

This talk explores how to build AI review systems that evaluate decisions like state ownership, component boundaries, and composition — and identify when those decisions signal misunderstanding, not just incorrectness.

Using a real system that reviews student pull requests, I’ll show the key design choices: grounding the LLM in curated mental models that encode why patterns matter, using deterministic rules to surface high-confidence signals before the LLM runs, and framing output as coaching questions rather than corrections.

Attendees will leave with a concrete framework for building review systems that develop judgment, not just code quality.

a.title: The invisible hand in your decisions: cognitive biases, heuristics, and AI
a.speaker: Vladi Stevanovic
a.desc:
The human brain is not a rational decision-making machine. It is a pattern-matching system equipped with shortcuts that work most of the time and fail in predictable, documentable ways.

This talk explores the cognitive biases and heuristics that influence how developers make technical decisions every day: from choice paralysis and decision fatigue to loss aversion, Miller's Law, and the IKEA effect. The patterns discussed in behavioral economics and cognitive psychology are playing out in your team standup, your architecture review, and your next tool evaluation... whether you notice them or not.

What most developers don't yet realize is that AI tools actively trigger many of these same shortcuts: automation bias, anchoring, the illusion of deliberation. The same brain that was already prone to these effects now has a highly confident, deeply agreeable assistant reinforcing them.

You'll leave knowing exactly what's happening in your brain (and in your AI chat) when you think you're making a rational decision.

b.title: AI patterns in Angular
b.speaker: Aristeidis Bampakos
b.desc: In this presentation, we will explore the latest advancements in AI for the Angular framework. First, we will learn how to utilize the Angular MCP server to automate processes and implement best practices during development. Next, we will discuss how to integrate Firebase AI Logic to create AI-assisted experiences in web applications. Finally, we will wrap up the presentation by offering tips on how to effectively approach AI in this rapidly evolving landscape.

a.title: Your agent has amnesia
a.speaker: Adam Cowley
a.desc:
You build an agent. It has a great conversation, learns something useful about the user, and makes a smart decision.

The next session brings an entirely different response. Sound familiar?

In this talk, we'll fix this problem and explore the three types of memory your agent needs in production.

Short-term memory so it can recall what was said earlier in a session.

Long-term memory so knowledge is accumulated across sessions.

Reasoning memory so you can inspect every decision it made and understand why.

We'll close by wrapping the whole thing in an MCP server - persistent agent memory, available to any client, wired up in minutes.

b.title: Generative UI for Production: How LLMs Compose Interfaces Within Your Design System
b.speaker: Konstantinos Leimonis
b.desc: Every generative UI demo starts from scratch, a chat bot streams a weather card, an AI generates a new app. But in production, you don't start from scratch. You have a component library, accessibility contracts, role-based permissions, and users who expect consistency. This talk explores the architecture for runtime generative UI inside an existing product. We'll cover how to expose your component library as a grammar the LLM can speak, how MCP Apps bridge AI capabilities to rendered interfaces, and the hard problems nobody's solving yet: non-determinism vs. design system contracts, permission-aware composition, and testing UI that's decided at request time. If you're evaluating how AI-composed interfaces fit into your product without a rewrite, this talk gives you the architecture, the constraints, and the incremental adoption path

a.title: Look, I Have a Runtime in My Browser
a.speaker: Theodore Vorillas
a.desc:
Browsers can also run Node.js. Sort of, with enough lies in the right places.
In this talk, we’ll build an almost-compatible Node.js runtime that lives entirely in the tab: no servers, no containers, no remote sandbox. We’ll stitch together Service Workers, VFS, and WebAssembly to fake the parts that matter, understand what breaks (and why), and see what surprisingly doesn’t.
Then we’ll hand that runtime to an agent: it writes code, runs it, reads the output, and iterates fully client-side.

b.title: Cue Lights and Go! Syncing Sound and Light with AI and React
b.speaker: Kathleen McMahon
b.desc: If you've ever worked backstage at an event, you know: timing matters. But what happens when sound, light, and interaction all need to synchronize? One missed cue and your symphony of sound and light becomes chaos. In this talk, we'll explore how React 19 and XState can orchestrate live cues across web APIs and AI-generated music, syncing it all with lighting. Pair this with the right hardware, and your room can come to life right on cue.

a.title: Building the AI-Native Workspace
a.speaker: Nestor Lopez
a.desc:
Most teams are adding AI through scattered surfaces: one chat app, one IDE assistant, one workflow bot, one knowledge tool, one automation runner. The result is powerful but fragmented. Context gets lost, permissions are inconsistent, and collaboration still happens around AI instead of with AI.

This talk explores the architecture of an AI-native workspace: one platform where humans, agents, conversations, documents, code, tools, terminals, and workflows live together. Based on building Zephyr AI Platform, we will look at the runtime underneath that idea: a Slack-like multi-threaded interface, specialist agents, AI orchestration, virtual filesystem tools, sandboxed execution, remote runtime streams, and benchmark gates for reusable AI specialists.

b.title: Vibes Don't Scale: Human-Driven Development in the Age of AI
b.speaker: Georgios Diamantopoulos
b.desc:
Low-code promised anyone could build software. It was true, until you hit a real wall: the blocks ran out, you needed custom code, you called an engineer.

Vibe coding has no visible wall. A founder used AI tools for six weeks and produced 300,000 lines of code; working UI, real users, flawless surface. Underneath: security holes, queries returning entire tables to count, and a codebase three engineers couldn't untangle.

He didn't know he'd hit the wall; it looked like a working product! The constraints appeared to disappear when they just shifted to security, maintainability, performance and UX.
Handing 300,000 lines to an engineering team and asking them to make it work — from experience — is borderline traumatic. You just devalued our entire careers by handing us this. Decades of perfecting a craft, dismissed by a chatbox.

Here's where it gets interesting. The map is not the territory — you have to build things to understand what you're building, and AI makes that exploration faster than ever. This is a skill issue — just not the one people think; the skill is recognising when the prototype became the product, and making sure it can bear the weight. That knowledge just went from nice-to-have to last line of defense.

Constraining AI before it writes, not after — that's what I call Human-Driven Development. Through live AI-assisted demos, I'll show how the tools engineers spent years mastering are the difference between software that ships and software that survives.

a.title: Building a Multi-Agent AI D&D with TypeScript
a.speaker: Muhammed Salih Güler
a.desc:
Ever wondered what happens when you give multiple AI agents different roles and let them collaborate? In this session, we’ll build a multi-agent system that creates and runs a Dungeons & Dragons campaign.

We’ll create an AI “Dungeon Master’s Guild” that connects to MCP servers (that we build ourselves) act as magical tools. We will have dice rollers, monster manuals, and character generators that agents discover dynamically. You’ll see live character creation, real-time world building with shared context, AI agents conversing via autonomous handoffs, and a complete D&D session where the audience becomes the adventuring party.

Learn multi-agent architecture, TypeScript patterns using tools, MCP integration, and best practices for orchestrating multiple AI models.

No D&D experience required – just bring your curiosity for AI and love of TypeScript!

b.title: Apps Are the New Tools
b.speaker: Pedro Rodrigues
b.desc:
Agents are moving beyond simple tool calls. The next step is bringing interactive apps directly into the conversation: rich, contextual interfaces that help people inspect, decide, and act without jumping between links, dashboards, and screenshots.

In this lightning talk, I’ll demo an incident response workflow that starts with a pager alert and moves through triage, investigation, resolution, postmortem drafting, and team celebration, all inside a shared agent session. Using a mocked incident environment inspired by real engineering workflows, I’ll show why apps are becoming the new tools agents use to turn conversation into action.

a.title: Who you gonna call? Slop-busters!
a.speaker: Dan Neciu
a.desc: Are you feeling overwhelmed by how much bad AI content you are seeing? Are your agents generating more and more SLOP? Are you hitting your token limits every day? In this talk, you will learn how AI slop shows up in different formats (text, image, code) and how to improve it by building a working harness around your coding agents to make them work better and use fewer tokens.

b.title: Building a real-time collaborative editor
b.speaker: Mihaela Gheorghe-Roman
b.desc:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to develop a solution similar to Google Docs and then build on top of it with extra layers of security and functionality?

During the planning phase of a military operation, there are multiple text documents that need to be updated simultaneously by multiple users. At the same time, there is a requirement to provide security in air-gapped deployments.

As such, a solution that follows high standards for security, performance and quality is required.

Within my presentation, I will be describing an embedded solution based on advanced operational transformation algorithms which allows real-time secure collaborative editing, as well as several challenges that we have faced during development and how we managed to overcome each of them.

a.title: The New Juniors Don't Know They're Juniors
a.speaker: Erasmo Hernandez
a.desc: AI made it possible for anyone to build software, creating two new kinds of juniors: builders with confidence but no knowledge to scale, and learners with knowledge but no confidence to start. This talk explores what each one needs, why senior engineers should be the bridge between them, and what seniors can learn from both.

a.title: Building a Multi-Step Agentic Image Generation Workflow
a.speaker: Jamund Ferguson
a.desc: My team at Stability AI built an agentic image-generation planning service using the Cloudflare Agents SDK and Cloudflare Workflows. Each step is shown to the user with human in the loop control and AI-based checks to ensure quality throughout the process. I'll walk you through the architecture, share what we learned shipping this to production and show you how to apply this technology to your own applications.

b.title: Microfrontends: Lessons Learned from Growing a Design System and Shared Libraries Across 20+ teams
b.speaker: Erasmo Hernandez
b.desc:
Scaling a microfrontends architecture across 20+ teams is challenging not just technically, but organizationally. In this talk, I’ll share the practical lessons learned from leading the growth of a large Design System and multiple shared libraries in a highly distributed environment. We’ll explore how to keep teams autonomous while maintaining consistency, how to evolve UI components and SDKs without breaking dozens of codebases, and which governance models actually work when hundreds of developers are contributing in parallel.

You’ll see real strategies for handling semantic versioning, coordinated releases, backward compatibility, and cross-team collaboration, as well as the pitfalls we encountered and the solutions that helped us move faster. Whether your organization is adopting microfrontends or already feeling the pain of scaling shared infrastructure, this session will give you actionable guidance to avoid bottlenecks, reduce friction, and build a healthier ecosystem. This is a talk built from real experience, real failures, and real wins designed to help you scale with confidence.

a.title: What! AI has access to my Node Environment! From MCP to Agents
a.speaker: Shivay Lamba
a.desc:
What will happen when AI is given access to a Node environment? Things get pretty interesting. It can has the capability to write code, install packages, generate files, and even launch servers. In this talk, you will learn how to build a Node.js Sandbox server powered by the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard that connects AI to real tools and data in a safe, controlled way.

The talk will walk through how the sandbox works: starting fresh Docker containers, installing npm packages on the fly, executing JavaScript, and sending back logs or files. Everything happens through simple MCP messages, allowing the AI to interact with your system just like a developer would, only faster.

You will see how this unlocks much more powerful use cases like generating charts with Chart.js, summarizing long articles from the web, creating and testing QR codes, scraping and saving content, generating PDFs and fake CSV data, or even spinning up mock APIs in seconds. By the end, you will know how to build your own MCP server and give your AI the keys to a real coding playground all thanks to LLMs ,AI and some nice Nodejs Magic

b.title: Harnessing AI to build your dream project
b.speaker: Moses Roth
b.desc: I'll tell the story of how I built an of AI harness to translate technical videos and all the things I learned along the way. Key insights will include proper planning and prompting, preventing AI laziness, avoiding AI slop, how your coding skills and perspective keep you valuable, and how to properly collaborate with both AI and other people.

a.title: Panel: The current State of JS and AI
a.speaker: Maximilian Schwarzmüller, Francesco Ciulla, Tejas Kumar, Evangelia Mitsopoulou, Dan Neciu
a.desc: This is a panel at the end of the conference to discuss what is the future, and how developers will progress to the new state of development. We have 4 of our big speakers coming to discuss what the changes will be and give us a more information on what to focus on.

a.title: Inside My Real Claude Code Workflow: Commands, Voice, Memory, and Building Your Own Agents
a.speaker: Yaroslav Matushevych
a.desc:
A walkthrough of my actual day-to-day Claude Code setup, ending with a working agent built live on stage.

I’ve been using Claude Code as part of my day-to-day engineering work, and this talk is a look at what that actually involves - the setup I’ve built around it, the decisions behind it, and some of the less obvious things that make the workflow work.

I’ll walk through custom slash commands and skills built around real work, voice dictation as a daily habit, and commands and features that are easy to overlook.

We’ll also get into context, memory and token efficiency: what gets pulled into a session, what can quietly pollute it, how CLAUDE.md and auto-memory fit together, what actually consumes context, and how to avoid wasting tokens. I’ll dig into what’s happening behind the scenes rather than treating context as a black box.

Then there’s the economics: when a fast, inexpensive model is enough, when a stronger one is worth it, and how prompt caching changes the trade-offs.

Finally, we’ll build a small working agent live, starting from an empty file. It will have its own tools, and I’ll show exactly what Claude sees when it decides whether to use them. I’ll deliberately give one of those tools a bad description and see what happens.

Expect real terminal output, practical techniques you can take back to your own workflow, and a live look at both what Claude Code can do and where you still need to keep your judgement switched on.

b.title: AI Governance for Engineers: Mapping Real Risk Under the EU AI Act
b.speaker: Christos Makris, Konstantinos Anagnostopoulos
b.desc: The EU AI Act is no longer a future problem: transparency duties already apply, general-purpose model obligations are in force, and the high-risk regime lands in 2027. This talk translates the regulation into something an engineer can act on — starting where the law starts, with the system rather than the model. Who is the provider and who is the deployer when you wrap someone else's API? What flips a chatbot into a high-risk classification? Which of your features already need disclosure, logging, or human oversight today? Then comes the part that matters: mapping real risk. Regulatory classification and engineering or business risk overlap, but they are not necessarily classified the same way.

a.title: How AI changes Supply Chain Security
a.speaker: Stella Varvarigou
a.desc:
Modern software supply chain attacks are no longer limited to malicious npm packages and compromised dependencies.

AI coding assistants, autonomous agents, MCP tools, and generated code are becoming part of the development pipeline - often with more trust than traditional dependencies ever had.

In this talk, we’ll explore how AI-assisted development introduces a new generation of supply chain risks:

• hallucinated or malicious packages,

• poisoned documentation,

• prompt injection,

• insecure generated code,

• and AI-driven dependency trust failures.

b.title: Zen and the art of skills maintenance
b.speaker: Beth Swingler
b.desc:
"To love without understanding harms the object of your love" (Thich Nhat Hanh)

For us, to code without understanding harms the product of our code -- our software. And quietly hollow out our own skills in the process. So how can you use AI as your coach, your teacher, and your partner in exploration? How can you prevent the brain rot of passivity? And when you're not writing it -- how can you keep all of the new code in your head?

This talk aims to ensure your favourite LLM makes you a better developer, not a worse one. I'll share a system for collaborating on software that leaves you sharper, more skilful, and still the one who understands what's running in production.

a.title: Panel: AI in Greek Business: Opportunities and Impact
a.speaker: Giorgos Tsiftsis, Maria Leontiou, Alexis Panousis, Dimitris Tsingos, Iro Tsakiri
a.desc: This panel explores how Artificial Intelligence is being adopted across Greek businesses and the ways it is reshaping industries, operations, and decision-making. Experts and industry leaders will discuss practical applications of AI, the benefits it can bring, such as increased efficiency, innovation, and competitivenessand the challenges organizations may face during adoption. The discussion will highlight how AI can support the growth of Greek businesses and what opportunities it creates for the future of work and the economy.

a.title: Goodbye slop; welcome determinism
a.speaker: David Khourshid
a.desc:
Vibe coding feels productive until you have to maintain it. Behind the agent "thinking..." you ignore and the code you never opened lies a growing pile of wasted tokens, nondeterministic behavior, and compounding errors hiding in plain sight.
This talk pushes back on the status quo: elaborate agent architectures, "prompting astrology", overnight automation loops burning through context windows and credit cards. We'll look at why determinism, state machines, and explicit guardrails aren't "old-school"... they're the only sustainable way forward.
We'll look at why vibe coding compounds technical debt faster than any era before it, and how modeling behavior explicitly lets you ship AI features you actually understand, maintain, and trust.

b.title: From Stack Overflow to LLMS: The Devaluation of Knowledge
b.speaker: Konstantinos Berdelis
b.desc:
The talk focuses on encouraging continuous learning and highlighting the importance of truly owning knowledge through the journey of a software developer progressing from Junior to Senior level.

It reflects on how things worked 7–8 years ago when I started my career: how you entered the world of knowledge, how you acquired it, and how you applied it to real-world codebases. Learning came from online documentation, Stack Overflow, online courses, educational platforms, and YouTube.

Fast forward to today, and we have entered the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), which can assist with code generation, debugging, troubleshooting, and even more.
But not thinking!

This talk raises important questions about where knowledge actually comes from, how we internalize and understand it, and how we ultimately apply it in practice. It explores the difference between receiving answers and truly understanding them, and the role that human reasoning still plays in software engineering.

The presentation concludes by discussing whether, in a world increasingly supported by LLMs, human knowledge is still necessary at the end of the day—and how that knowledge can continue to be effectively applied to solve real problems.

a.title: AI & Devs: Adopting To A New Reality
a.speaker: Maximilian Schwarzmüller
a.desc: Four years after ChatGPT’s release and 18 months after Claude Code, AI is changing the role of developers and the skills we need at an increasing rate. I’ll look ahead from the perspective of someone who is not only trying to adapt to that change, but also helping others develop the right skills and mindset.
